question.text: A radar sends an electromagnetic signal of electric field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> which strikes a target on line of sight at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> in a medium. After that, a part of signal (echo) reflects back towards the radar with same velocity and by same path. If the signal was transmitted at time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> from radar, then after how much time echo will reach to the radar?

solution.text:
The speed of light is given by,

c=E0 B0=2.251.5×10-8=1.5×108 m s-1

Therefore, time taken for the echo will be,

t=2dc=6×1031.5×108=4×10-5 s
